types.Bat: A cave bat that hangs waiting, then flies along an invisible rail and dives at whatever it runs into: no line of sight, just touch. One brush is enough for the whole colony: the first Bat to find a target sets every Bat in the game on it at once. Each attacks once, flies up and is gone, and none survives a screen change.
types.BeeSwarmHole: A hole that pumps out a fresh bee swarm on a timer, forever, while you stand on its screen. Parking the rolling boulder over it plugs it: the game checks for a RollingBall covering the hole before every spawn. The game places exactly one, in the Paramonian Temple.
types.Bees: A wasps' nest, though the game's files call them wasps and players call them bees. A few drift around it harmlessly; trip its switch and it boils over into an angry swarm that hunts you until its chase timer runs out, stinging everything it envelops on the way. When the swarm dies the nest writes its own switch back off and re-arms.
types.CrawlingSlig: A Slig with no legs, dragging itself along the floor: no gun, no attack, just a desperate crawl toward a locker where it stands up armed. Every one the game fields starts asleep, and half wake straight into the scramble; their panic switch is the always-on id 1. Its crawl direction is decided once, when it spawns, and Random is a single coin flip rather than wandering.
types.CrawlingSligButton: A floor button only a player-driven Crawling Slig can press: Abe can't, and a crawling slig's own AI never looks for one. The game places exactly one, and pressing it always makes a noise Sligs and Slogs hear, whatever its switch does.
types.EnemyStopper: An invisible fence for creatures: Abe walks straight through, while patrols and chases stop, turn or give up at its line, each creature its own way. Its switch gate is inverted between the games: an Oddysee stopper blocks while its switch is off, an Exoddus one while it is on, so the permanent fence reads switch_id 0 in Oddysee and 1 in Exoddus.
types.Fleech: A legless carnivore that sleeps until noise wakes it, then crawls after you faster than Abe can walk and drags its catch in with its tongue. Waking is an anger meter, not a trigger: walking feeds it, sneaking is genuinely silent. Only one Fleech in a level can eat at a time; the rest queue. It is one of the few things in either game that can eat a Mudokon.
types.FlyingSlig: A Slig in a hover rig, patrolling an invisible overhead rail and lobbing grenades (never bullets) at what it spots below. It hangs from a collision line rather than flying free, and only leaves the rail while possessed; hold the chant to let go and it blows itself up rather than hand the rig back. Unlike its walking cousin it ignores bound ids, leashing to whatever posts sit near its rail's ends.
types.FlyingSligSpawner: An invisible watcher that materialises one Flying Slig when its switch turns on, re-arming when that slig dies. Its fields are the stat sheet of the slig it will produce (the block is byte-identical to a placed Flying Slig's), and it writes its own switch back off on the slig's death, so anything else wired to the id sees the drop.
types.Glukkon: In Exoddus, the industrialist boss class: he cannot hurt you at all. He screams, and his scream writes a switch that summons what can. Possess him and his voice commands Sligs; three placements are the named executives with their own movie deaths. Oddysee's six Glukkons are something else entirely: scenery behind the Board Room glass, jeering until the ending Shrykulls them.
types.Greeter: A wheeled security machine sweeping a motion-detector beam ahead of itself. Cross the beam while moving and it charges and electrocutes; hold still and it rolls past. It carries its own detector rather than answering a placed one, and its start direction is wired backwards: Left starts it rolling right.
types.HoneyDripTarget: A single aiming dot: the hanging honey sack in its camera drips its honey exactly here. Only one exists, under the Paramonia hive Elum can't leave alone. The game's other honey sack has no target anywhere in its level, so its drips land unseen at the path's corner.
types.Paramite: A spider-crab that hisses a warning before it charges, and drops in on a silk thread from off-screen. Thrown meat distracts an idle one but never one already chasing; alone it hesitates, with another Paramite on the screen it commits. In Exoddus it can be possessed and climbs the web lines, and it obeys a possessed Paramite's calls: Paramites listen to Paramites, never to Abe.
types.ParamiteWebLine: The hanging web strand a Paramite climbs, but only its artwork. The climbable part is a track line the level already carries; the strand finds that line, drapes itself along it, and wobbles when a Paramite grabs on. Abe can't touch it: riding one means possessing a Paramite. All 25 hang in Mudomo Vault.
types.Scrab: A two-legged carnivore that paces between its bound posts and kills what it reaches in one hit. Two Scrabs that see each other fight, and the duel is decided by which one's turn comes first in the engine's update order, not by strength. In Exoddus Abe can possess one; finishing a howl charges the spin attack, and spending it costs the charge.
types.ScrabLeftBound: The left end of a ground creature's beat: pace into it and turn back. Unlike a Slig's posts these carry no id (a creature takes whichever bound it walks into), and only the patrol honours them; a chasing Scrab crosses its own leash freely. In Exoddus they pen more than Scrabs: Glukkons, Greeters and Slurgs all turn at them, and 23 of the 56 pairs sit in levels with no Scrab at all.
types.ScrabNoFall: Despite the name it doesn't forbid falling: it authorises jumping. A chasing Scrab takes a running leap at the end of its ground when its prey is level with it, or when one of these markers sits ahead saying jump anyway; with neither, it runs off the edge and falls. Only the chase reads it.
types.ScrabRightBound: The right end of a ground creature's beat: pace into it and turn back. It carries no id and pairs with no particular creature, so the patrolling Scrab (or, in Exoddus, Glukkon, Greeter or Slurg) simply turns at whichever post it meets, and a chase crosses it freely.
types.ScrabSpawner: A switch-triggered Scrab factory carrying a full Scrab stat sheet of its own. It keeps exactly one Scrab in flight at a time: the next spawns only when the last is gone, the spawner writing its own switch back off in between. The game fields exactly one, in Mudanchee Vault.
types.SlapLock: A shuddering spirit lock that only Abe's slap can break. Ghost-guarded ones free a spirit that flies to the tomb door named by one target field and sets the switch named by the other on arrival; a broken lock holding the invisibility power-up respawns as a permanent dispenser of it.
types.Slig: The gun-toting guard on stilts, the games' signature enemy: it patrols between its bound posts and shoots what it sees on its own plane of the world. Its start_state is the field to read, and the value labelled listening is really a stationary sentry: it holds its post and fires the moment you step in front of it. A sleeping one snores audibly from the neighbouring screen (the ambience is read straight off this marker before any Slig exists), and a blast reaching the marker kills it sight unseen, the gibs flying in from off-screen.
types.SligBoundLeft: The left post of a Slig's patrol pen: a Slig carrying the matching id turns short of this post's line and never walks past it. The post does two quieter jobs too: it loads the Slig animation sets for its camera, and it can conjure its matching Slig onto your screen from a camera away, which is how one walks in from off-screen.
types.SligBoundRight: The right post of a Slig's patrol pen: a Slig carrying the matching id turns short of this post's line and never walks past it. Both games place slightly fewer right posts than left, so some Sligs are fenced on one side only.
types.SligGetPants: A locker of Slig trousers: a Crawling Slig that reaches it climbs in and walks out a full armed Slig. The locker's own fields are the stat sheet of the Slig it produces (the transformation reads them, not the crawler's), and if the crawler was possessed, you carry over into the new body.
types.SligGetWings: A locker stocked with a hover rig instead of trousers. The Crawling Slig that reaches it flies out as a Flying Slig, drifting upward until it catches a rail to latch onto; its fields are that slig's stat sheet, and the game fields exactly one.
types.SligPersist: A leash pin that keeps a Slig alive off-camera. A Slig sharing its id survives while any of its pins is on the current screen, instead of despawning when it walks out of view; Exoddus leans on these harder than Oddysee, placing more pins than it places Sligs.
types.SligSpawner: A marked spot that materialises a Slig when its switch turns on, and since its field block is a Slig's, a spawner tells you exactly what is coming. In Oddysee every spawner is single-shot; in Exoddus 30 of the 32 re-arm each time their slig dies, writing the switch back off as they do. Spawner Sligs skew hard toward Chase, a start state placed Sligs barely use: spawners are how the games deliver Sligs that arrive already hunting.
types.Slog: The slavering guard dog with a fatal bite. Its three anger fields stack as increments (wake at wake_up_anger, bark that much plus bark_anger, charge past the sum of all three) fed by noise, speech and Abe standing close; one thrown-object hit adds the whole charge threshold at once. A Slig (which is to say, you possessing one) can whistle it to heel or set it on someone with "get 'em", the only way its own search ever picks out a Slig; a spawner-born Slog simply hunts whatever you are possessing.
types.SlogHut: Not a hut and not a Slog: a particle emitter puffing sleep-Zs while its switch is off. Every one in the game shares its switch with a SlogSpawner: the Zs mark the kennel while the switch is off, and the moment it flips the Zs stop and the paired spawner starts pouring out Slogs.
types.SlogSpawner: A Slog fountain: while its switch is on it releases Slogs on a timer, up to a lifetime quota that survives leaving the screen. Its at-a-time cap counts every live Slog, not just its own (neighbouring spawners share one ceiling), and each Slog it births arrives already hunting, on fixed anger numbers rather than a placed Slog's.
types.Slurg: A fat slug that inches along the floor and bursts with a wet pop under anyone's step: Abe's, a Mudokon's, a Slig's, a Scrab's. It can't hurt anything; the danger is the pop itself, a loud noise, and loud noises are what wake Fleeches. Its switch field is a kill counter (each burst adds one), and eleven Slurgs ship wired to one.
types.SlurgSpawner: A crack that dribbles out Slurgs on a timer, up to a lifetime quota that survives leaving the screen: a spawner that has met its five stays spent. The game places exactly one, in Mudanchee Vault, wired to the always-on switch: it never stops until the quota is met.
types.ZBall: A pendulum swinging toward and away from the camera, in front of Abe and then behind him. Its damage rides the animation itself: only frames the artists marked can hit. Its start position (centre, out, in) staggers a row of balls out of phase. All six in the game hang in the Paramonian Temple.
types.ZSligCover: A no-fire zone for depth shooting: inside this rectangle a background Slig cannot snipe across the depth axis, and a Z-bullet that lands there is absorbed. It protects both ways (a Slig standing in cover won't fire out of it) but only whole-body: a box that half-covers you protects you not at all.
types.ZzzSpawner: A floating snore: it puffs a sleep-Z on a timer, knowing nothing about who sleeps below, so the author parks it over the sleeper. Its switch gate is inverted: Zs flow while the switch is off and stop when it turns on, which is why the sleeper's wake switch and the spawner's can be one number.
